rationale:
features_open/035 P1 direction 2 was WRITTEN, council-reviewed over three rounds, committed on 2026-08-31 (3fd617ef6, fdb03cbc1) — and never called. This wires it, and fixes the three defects that wiring exposed.

THE PROBLEM. `recomposeAncestors` re-renders a composition parent after one of its children is edited. Without it a child edit is invisible on the page it just changed, because a composed page serves the TOPMOST ancestor's bytes, not the child's. It has sat with zero callers since it landed. A fully-controlled binary probe on 2026-09-02 found the symbol ABSENT from the running chassis (v1.0.1355) while its sibling symbols were present — Go's linker eliminates a function nothing calls.

WHY IT HAD NO CALLER, and this is the finding. Its signature demanded `tx *sql.Tx`, justified by a paragraph in its own file header headed 'THE db/tx SPLIT IS FORCED, not stylistic', reasoning about which reads must see 'the uncommitted edit' inside apply_section_edit's transaction. THERE IS NO SUCH TRANSACTION. [MEASURED 2026-09-03] `grep -nE 'BeginTx|\.Begin\(|Commit\(\)|Rollback\(\)' platform/orchestration/actions/section_editor_actions.go` returns NOTHING; that action persists through `updatePageComponentAfterEdit(ctx, params.DB, ...)` on the autocommit connection, like every other write on the path. So the parameter could not be supplied by the one caller it was designed for. Three rounds of PLAN review did not surface it; attempting the wiring did, in one grep. Nothing type-checks a comment.

The guarantee the tx was there to provide arrives for free: the child's UPDATE has committed before the recompose runs, so an ordinary read sees it. Every read now goes through *sql.DB.

THREE DEFECTS THE WIRING EXPOSED, all in the ancestor write:
(1) UNGUARDED. It was a bare `UPDATE page_components SET rendered_html = ... WHERE id = $1` — no tombstone predicate, no lock predicate. Both are on every other write in the edit path. This matters more here than there: a recompose is a MECHANICAL consequence of a child edit, so it reaches rows nobody chose. ApplySectionEditAction checks the lock (bugs_open/058) and the tombstone (bugs_open/360) on the row it was ASKED to edit and on nothing above it. Without these clauses, the one code path in the estate that can rewrite a human-locked section is the one path no human pointed at it. Nothing existing would have caught the absence: TestNoHandSpelledTombstonePredicate finds a WRONG spelling, never a MISSING one, and page_component_writer_coverage_test.go asks only about the floors (which this writer did already enforce).
(2) ZERO ROWS AFFECTED READ AS SUCCESS. The statement succeeds whether or not a predicate admitted the row, so an unchecked result reports a refused ancestor as recomposed — a green result over stale bytes, which is this feature's own defect class arriving inside its fix.
(3) UNSTAMPED. page_components.rendered_html is archived by the 357/552 triggers, and bugs_open/355 A1 exists so those archive rows name the writer instead of the connection's socket. Six writers stamp today; this was a seventh writer of the same column that did not.

INTENT AND BLAST RADIUS. This ships inert. [MEASURED 2026-09-03] 0 of 3,229 page_components rows carry a parent_instance_id, and 0 of 386 content_components declare a slots block, so `hierarchyAncestorChain` returns empty on its first read and the loop body is unreachable on today's data. The cost added to the live edit path is ONE indexed SELECT of parent_instance_id per edit. That is RFC_022's shape exactly: opt-in, unsafe side OFF, inert until a row opts in — the 2026-08-11 owner ruling says that shape is not architecture-scope, and 035 section 7 already measured it against all three conditions.

OTHER CONSUMERS OF THE SEAM, named rather than merely measured (2026-07-29 owner ruling item 3): the only consumer of apply_section_edit's result map is the section-editor workflow, and this ADDS a key (`stale_ancestor_slots`) rather than changing one. The only consumers of page_components.rendered_html writes are the archive triggers, and this change makes its writes MORE attributable, not less. No existing key, statement or return shape changes.

WHAT IS NOT IN THIS CHANGE, deliberately: the READ path. `walkComponentHierarchy` still has no production caller, so a row that opted in today would still render flat. That is the rest of P1 and it is a separate submission — hazard 6.9 (loadStoredSections has no parent_instance_id filter, so a nested walk would mis-attach per-section figures) must land inside that change, not this one.

plan.summary: Wire features_open/035 P1 direction 2. Remove the `tx *sql.Tx` parameter that no caller could supply (apply_section_edit holds no transaction — measured), call recomposeAncestors from ApplySectionEditAction after the persist and before the reassembly, and give its ancestor write the three protections it lacked: the tombstone and lock predicates, a RowsAffected check that reads zero as a refusal, and the A1 writer stamp. Four mutation-proved tests, and a stale concept-register claim corrected.

edits.rationale: Drop the unsatisfiable tx parameter; move the ancestor write into its own function so the guard tests can drive it directly (the seam section_editor_tombstone_guard_test.go uses on updatePageComponentAfterEdit); add the two predicates, the RowsAffected refusal and the writer stamp. The file header's 'db/tx split is FORCED' paragraph is replaced by the measurement that refutes it, kept visible as a correction rather than deleted. ALSO CHANGED, comment-only and therefore not a separate edit (097 refuses a comment-only sketch, correctly): platform/orchestration/actions/component_hierarchy_walk.go repeats the same false claim on the hierarchyDB interface — 'so the render paths and apply_section_edit's transaction share one implementation'. The interface is right and stays; the justification is refuted, so it carries a dated correction. Zero code lines change in that file.

The call site. Placement is load-bearing on both sides: AFTER the persist so ancestors embed the new child bytes (and because the child write has committed, so an ordinary read sees it), and BEFORE assemblePage, which reads page_components back — recomposing after it would ship the stale parent in the very HTML this action returns for deployment. The stale slots are published in the result map so an ancestor that could not be refreshed is queryable in collected_data rather than living only in a pod log that rotates within minutes.

A distinct writer name, not a reuse of section_editor.update: the child write and the ancestor rewrite are two different decisions inside one action, and an archive that conflated them could not answer 'who rewrote the parent'.

The file had no test at all. Four cases, each mutation-proved at authoring time and the mutations recorded in the file header: M1 drop the tombstone predicate, M2 drop the lock predicate, M3 return true instead of n > 0, M4 delete the call from ApplySectionEditAction — all four KILLED their case. The wiring case strips Go comments before scanning, because this file and the call site both name the function in prose and an unstripped scan would pass vacuously; its weakness (it proves the call is written, not that it executes) is stated in the file, and the behavioural half is the inert-row case, which asserts via sqlmock that NOTHING beyond one SELECT runs on a top-level row.

Cited here because the rationale names it. CLC-030's relations line told every reader that 'page_components.parent_instance_id is read by ZERO Go files and set on 0 of 2,005 rows as of 2026-08-24'. The reachability half is now false — the membership queries are reached in production from ApplySectionEditAction — so it is corrected with strike-through and re-measured (0 of 3,229 as of 2026-09-03; the table grew ~1,000 rows in three days while the parented count stayed at zero). The standing advice it gives is unchanged; only its reason is.

features_open/035 section 7: composition is opt-in, the unsafe default is OFF, and zero live consumers name it — the three RFC_022 conditions, and the 2026-08-11 owner ruling that this shape is not architecture-scope.
plan.risks: 1) THE ONE BEHAVIOURAL CHANGE ON A LIVE PATH is one extra indexed SELECT per section edit (hierarchyAncestorChain reads parent_instance_id for the edited row). On today's data it returns NULL and the loop body never runs — 0 of 3,229 rows are parented [MEASURED 2026-09-03] — so the recompose itself is unreachable. A reviewer should check that claim rather than accept it: the query is a primary-key lookup and the early return is `if !parent.Valid || parent.String == "" { return chain, nil }`. 2) recomposeAncestors CANNOT return an error by design, so a broken ancestor cannot fail a child edit. The cost of that choice is that a persistently unrefreshable ancestor is reported and not escalated; today nothing consumes `stale_ancestor_slots`, and a reviewer may reasonably say the consumer should exist before composition goes live. It cannot exist usefully before there is a composed page. 3) The lock predicate is NEW authority in the conservative direction: a locked ancestor is now left stale rather than overwritten. That is fail-closed but it means a composed page with a locked parent can serve an out-of-date parent indefinitely. The alternative — refusing the whole child edit when an ancestor is locked — is a sharper change to a live path and is deliberately not taken here. 4) enforceSingleSlotFloors gains a second caller with no calibration of its own against composed parents, because none exist. A floor breach REFUSES that ancestor rather than erroring, which bounds the uncalibrated risk to staleness. The calibration harness should be re-run when composed pages exist. 5) The wiring test is a source scan and therefore proves the call is written, not that it executes; the behavioural half is the sqlmock inert-row case. A reviewer should judge whether that pair is enough, given the alternative is mocking the whole render chain.
